Tools most coding agents ship with:
Returns a file's contents as a tool result
Creates or edits a file in the
Runs a shell command and returns its output
Finds files or text matching a pattern across the codebase
A tool is defined by three things: a name, a description of what it does, and a schema for its parameters. The harness sends these definitions to the
with every request, and the model chooses a tool the same way it produces everything else — by writing
, in this case a structured call with arguments. The model never executes anything itself; the harness reads the call, runs the function, and sends back the result.

The tool list sets what the agent can do. A capable model with a narrow tool set is a narrow agent: it will route everything through whatever it has, which is why agents lean so heavily on Bash — a shell is one tool that reaches most of the system.
